Q: How do I code without being completely dependent on AI? A:

AI may be faster, but the quality, maintainability, and educational value of AI assisted programs is worse. As a young person trying to establish yourself, I would focus on craft and long term productivity. This will require a lot of struggle and will seem slow, especially compared to your peers who are using AI a lot, but the end result will be better. A good example of this attitude in action is the zig programming language, which has banned AI contributions and is intent on taking as long as they need to get to 1.0.

Personally, as an intermediate developer who is sometimes under a lot of time pressure, I apply a barbell strategy to AI - I spend half of my time coding and debugging from hand (only downloaded documentation, often offline), and half of my time coding with AI assistance (chat window mostly). I usually do it in time windows - I block all AI stuff before lunch and then use AI after lunch. If I'm learning a library or language I will do everything by hand. I use AI less if I don't have strict deadlines, and more if I need to quickly create something, but this leads to technical debt.

Through this strategy I feel like I can stay aware of current tools without losing the ability to code - but as you are someone who is learning, I would err on the side of using AI less than me.

Q: Group by using COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY A:

Your use of a window function appears to be misplaced. The expected output in the question has a column (lossmeanbyco) which is completely undefined, so let's just remove that from the question. No detail was specified.

The original tables are undefined, so let's just take your question input (which isn't input at all) and make a new table called "test" containing that data.

Test case

CREATE TABLE test ( cst  varchar(5), st  varchar(5),  co  varchar(5) );

INSERT INTO test VALUES
  ('sal'          , 'pa'              ,  'ctr')
, ('sal'          , 'pa'              ,  'ctr')
, ('sal'          , 'pa'              ,  'est')
, ('sal'          , 're'              ,  'ctr')
, ('sal'          , 're'              ,  'ctr')
, ('sal'          , 're'              ,  'ust')
, ('cus'          , 'pa'              ,  'ctr')
, ('cus'          , 're'              ,  'ctr')
, ('cus'          , 're'              ,  'ctr')
, ('cus'          , 're'              ,  'ctr')
;

The result column count is easily generated with simple aggregation:

SELECT cst
     , st
     , co
     , COUNT(*) AS count
  --mean of loss by co
  FROM test
 WHERE st != 'te'
 GROUP  BY cst,st ,co  -- , count
 ORDER BY cst , st, co
;

The result:

cst st co count
cus pa ctr 1
cus re ctr 3
sal pa ctr 2
sal pa est 1
sal re ctr 2
sal re ust 1

This seems to be about all that can be done with the limited detail provided.

Q: sybase while loop assistance A:

I found the following statement which occurs twice a little odd:

SELECT @rowsaf = @@rowcount FROM #MyTemp

I would use :

SELECT @rowsaf = count(*) FROM #MyTemp

@@rowcount is a system variable that stores the number of records affected by the most recent executable command. It's not related to count of rows in a table.
See if this brings you closer to desired result. A UNION statement with 1 sql per code value is definitely not recommended.

Q: Functionality of a mobile browser build from scratch A:

That is a JS library. Having a browser support it by design is a native implementation. What are you actually asking? Of course anything is possible, but as Greg said, it can be a "yes" or "no". Even if a browser supported it, doesn't that mean a mobile web app needs to also support it? And if the mobile web app supports it (for example cos it uses PressureJS), why would there be a need for the browser to natively support it? Either we are missing something or your question is too vague.

Q: tool for generated design Rent Car Website A:

I checked the site, and honestly, I would not rebuild everything with an AI design tool.

The structure is already quite good. You already have the important parts: booking form, car list, service information, testimonials, FAQs, and WhatsApp contact options. The site also performs well in Lighthouse, so a complete redesign may create more risk than benefit.

The main thing I noticed is the hero section. The slogan and call-to-action do not stand out enough because they sit on top of a strong background image. On some screen sizes, the text becomes harder to read. I also checked it with a contrast extension and found several text/background combinations with low contrast.

That matters more than people think. A visitor should understand your service in a few seconds: car rental in Palembang, available options, and how to book. Right now, the visual style looks nice, but the main message does not hit strongly enough.

I would start by improving the hero instead of replacing the whole site. Add a darker overlay behind the text, use a more controlled gradient, or place the text inside a solid or semi-solid content area. Make the main headline more direct, for example:

“Rental Mobil Palembang – Dengan Sopir atau Lepas Kunci”

Then place one clear action below it, such as “Book via WhatsApp” or “Check Available Cars”.

AI can still be useful, but I would use it only for exploring layout ideas or creating a quick prototype. Do not let an AI tool replace the existing site without checking accessibility, mobile behavior, SEO structure, and booking flow.

In my opinion, this site does not need a full AI-generated redesign. It needs a focused conversion and accessibility improvement, especially in the hero section and any low-contrast text areas.
